review_notes: I read the whole file and compared its proofs against each other. I read the PoleOrder lemmas (lines 142-197) and the Dictionary lemmas (lines 736-830) in full. The other repeated pieces are short: the `Subsingleton.elim` on `comp` of ring homs, and the "ℓ ∣ 1 is false" arguments at about lines 78-87 and 560-566. I judged those too small to count as repeated machinery. The Vieta, irreducibility, and swapBivar blocks each appear once. I did not compile anything. The proposed refactor relies on `coeff_aeval_jq_neg` being stated for `m : ℕ` with `P.natDegree ≤ m`, so `le_rfl` instantiates it at `m = P.natDegree`. I also assume `coeff_jq_pow_self` and `coeff_jq_pow_of_lt` are available at the earlier position, which is true because they are exported before both sites.

findings.excerpt:
private theorem coeff_aeval_jq_neg_natDegree (P : Polynomial ℚ) :
    (Polynomial.aeval jq P).coeff (-(P.natDegree : ℤ)) = P.coeff P.natDegree := by
findings.problem: The file proves the same pole-order coefficient fact twice. `coeff_aeval_jq_neg_natDegree` computes the coefficient of q^{-natDegree P} in `aeval jq P` by `Finset.sum_eq_single`. The top term gives `coeff_jq_pow_self` and `mul_one`. The lower terms vanish by `coeff_jq_pow_of_lt` with `omega`. Lines 745-760 repeat this almost verbatim as `coeff_aeval_jq_neg`, with `m ≥ natDegree P` in place of `natDegree P`. They add one extra branch for the case where the index is absent from the range. The first lemma is exactly the instance `m := P.natDegree` of the second. Two copies of the same sum-splitting proof must be maintained together, and a reader cannot tell the later one generalises the earlier.
findings.proposed_change: Keep only the general lemma. Move `coeff_aeval_jq_neg (P : Polynomial ℚ) {m : ℕ} (hm : P.natDegree ≤ m) : (Polynomial.aeval jq P).coeff (-(m : ℤ)) = P.coeff m` up to just before `namespace PhiGen` (for example next to `evalAtJ_injective`). It sits in the `ModularCurve` namespace, so both the PoleOrder section and the Dictionary section can use it. Its proof is the existing one from lines 745-760. Then delete lines 153-165 and replace the two uses at lines 185 and 191 with `coeff_aeval_jq_neg P le_rfl`. This has the same type, since `((P.natDegree : ℕ) : ℤ)` is what `m := P.natDegree` gives. `natDegree_eq_of_aeval_jq_eq_jqN` and `monic_of_aeval_jq_eq_jqN` then keep their current proofs. `coeff_aeval_jq_of_lt` can stay beside it. The Dictionary uses at lines 772 and 783 are unchanged, since they refer to the same lemma, now defined earlier.
findings.benefit: This removes a roughly 13-line duplicate of a non-trivial sum-splitting argument. Only one proof of the leading-pole-coefficient computation remains. The Dictionary section and the PoleOrder section visibly share one API. Any later change to `coeff_jq_pow_*` or to the `aeval` expansion needs fixing in one place.
